inbox.subject: Board week: deck v4 by Wednesday
inbox.body:
Alex,

Quick note to start board week. The board meets Friday the 20th. I need the next version of the deck from you by Wednesday end of day so I can get it to the board members Thursday morning.

Open items on my side: the year end view still shows $17.8M ARR against the $19.0M plan, a $1.2M gap. I will keep that framing unless Harborline timing moves. I would like a hiring slide from Jordan, given what she is seeing.

Working session is on the calendar for 2:30pm today.

Julian

inbox.subject: Hiring pipeline down 17 percent, Q1 care lead plan at risk
inbox.body:
Alex,

Heads up before our 1:1. Our active hiring pipeline is down 17 percent month over month. Care lead applicants are the bulk of the drop, mostly Boston and Philadelphia.

The Q1 care lead plan is at risk. We planned 12 new care leads starting by end of March. We have 3 accepted offers and not enough people in late stages to close the rest at our normal conversion. That matters for Harborline: today we can set up 800 households from January 1 and keep the promise, against 1,600 on a full launch.

I want to talk through adding a second recruiting partner and a referral bonus. I can draft the board slide.

Jordan

inbox.subject: Postmortem: Boston overnight backlog (please read before 9:30am)
inbox.body:
Team,

Attached is the written postmortem for the Boston overnight incident. Summary: the handoff queue stalled for 3.2 hours, backlog peaked at 164 handoffs and was down to 58 by 5am. Root cause was a retry loop in the provider confirmation sync that blocked the queue worker instead of failing over. No missed safety items, per Dr. Patel's review.

Fixes, monitoring changes and owners are in section 4. Priya has asked for the queue fix to be prioritized; details from her separately.

Sanjay

inbox.subject: Urgent patch for the queue issue, roadmap impacted by 1 week
inbox.body:
Alex,

Following Sanjay's postmortem, I've asked engineering to take on the queue worker patch and the failover change as urgent work this sprint. I don't want to ship Harborline onboarding on top of the current behavior.

The cost: the roadmap is impacted by 1 week. Partner portal improvements and the Self reminders release each move out by one week. Harborline onboarding dates do not move.

I'd like your OK at the 9:30am so the team can start today. I will update the roadmap slide for Julian's deck.

Priya

inbox.subject: VP of Care search: starting again
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for the candid debrief last week. We are ready to begin the VP of Care search again. For our 11:30am I'll bring a revised profile with more weight on multi-site operations and scaling a care team through a large employer launch, plus a fresh target list of about 30 names.

Realistic timeline is first conversations in early December and a shortlist before the holidays. Please let me know if anyone besides Jordan should join.

Best,
Grace Lindqvist
TalentBridge

inbox.subject: Open-weight model test: on track
inbox.body:
Alex,

Short update ahead of 1:30pm. The open-weight model test is on track. Week one numbers on the replay set are close to our current model on task closure, and latency is better. Week two runs on live shadow traffic with no member-facing output. Nadia signed off on the data handling.

I'll have a recommendation by the end of next week.

Wen

newsletters.title: Employers widen caregiving benefits for 2027
newsletters.body: Benefits leaders report more caregiving support in 2027 plan designs, with navigation services leading. Analysts flag activation and staffing as the main risks for vendors scaling into large employers.

newsletters.title: Open-weight models close the gap on structured tasks
newsletters.body: New evaluations show open-weight models approaching closed models on structured workflow tasks, with lower serving costs. The authors caution that eval sets rarely match production traffic.
